overall: The AG found neither the Boston Bikes Program, its director, nor the Boston Bicycle Advisory Board is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law, so no violation; matter closed.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Boston Bikes Program and its director failed to post notice of an April 28, 2011 North End meeting on the Harbor Bikes plan.
allegations.key_passage: We find that neither the BBP, Ms. Freedman, nor the BBAB violated the Open Meeting Law, as none is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Boston Bikes Program and its director failed to post notice of a June 6, 2011 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the BBP is not a multiple-member board, it cannot be a public body.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Boston Bicycle Advisory Board did not properly notice its June 7, 2011 meeting as required by the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Because the BBAB is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law, it did not violate the law by failing to post notice of its June 7, 2011 meeting.
